body.text: Antarvyāptisamarthanam /
body.translated_text: <s>Antarvyāptisamarthana</s> (Establishment of Internal Pervasion)

body.text: om namo buddhāya /
body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: iha sattvamarthakriyākāritvaṃ taditarasattvalakṣaṇāyogāt / tacca kramayaugapadyābhyāṃ vyāptaṃ parasparavyavacchedalakṣaṇatvādanayoḥ / prakārāntareṇa karaṇāsambhavāt / kramayaugapadye cākṣaṇikatve na staḥ / pūrvvāparakālayoaravicalitaikasvabhāvasya karttṛtvākarttṛtve virudvadharmmadvayāyogāt /
body.translated_text: Here, existence (<s>sattva</s>) is [defined as] causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), because of the impossibility of any other definition of existence. And that [causal efficacy] is pervaded by [either] succession (<s>krama</s>) or simultaneity (<s>yaugapadya</s>), since these two are defined by mutual exclusion. Because production is not possible in any other manner. And succession and simultaneity do not exist in what is non-momentary (<s>akṣaṇika</s>), because for something that has one and the same nature in the earlier and later moments, the contradictory pair of properties — being an agent and not being an agent — is impossible.

body.text: tatra na tāvat kramaḥ kramāṇāmekaikaṃ prati pūrvāparakālayoḥ karttṛtvākarttṛtvāpatteḥ / evaṃ sarvvakramābhāvāt kevalaṃ sakalakāryyayaugapadyamavaśiṣyate / tatra ca sphuṭa taraḥ pūrvvāparakālayoḥ karttṛtvākartṛtvaprasaṅgaḥ / virudve ca karttṛtvākarttṛtve ekadharmmiṇi na sambhavataḥ / ekasvabhāvaśca tāvatkālamakṣaṇika iti sidva etasmin kramayaugapadyayorayogaḥ / tadevamakṣaṇike vyāpakānupalabdhyā niṣidvaṃ sattvaṃ kṣaṇika evā[va] tiṣṭhate iti kṣaṇikatvena vyāptaṃ / tattena vyāptaṃ yat yatra dharmmiṇi sidhyati tatra kṣaṇikatvaṃ prasādhayati / idamevedānīṃ vicāryyate / keyaṃ (kveyaṃ) vyāptigrahītavyā dṛṣṭāntadharmmiṇi sādhyadharmmiṇi vā / kecidāhuḥ / dṛṣṭāntadharmmiṇyeva dhūmavat / anyathā sādhanavaiphalyaṃ syāt / ubhayadharmmasidvi(dve)ranāntarīyakatvāt vyāptisidveḥ / nahi mahānasasidvāyāmagnidhūmayorvyāptau punaragnisidvaye dhūmaliṅgamanviṣyata iti / tathāhi /
body.translated_text: In that regard: first, succession [is impossible for the non-momentary], because for each of the successive [moments], the consequence of being an agent and not being an agent at the earlier and later moments would follow. Thus, in the absence of all succession, only the simultaneity of all effects remains. And in that case, the consequence of being an agent and not being an agent at the earlier and later moments is even more obvious. And the contradictory [properties of] being an agent and not being an agent cannot belong to a single substratum (<s>dharmin</s>). And something that has a single nature is non-momentary for that duration — this being established, the impossibility of both succession and simultaneity [for the non-momentary] is proven. Thus, existence, which has been negated in the non-momentary by the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>), remains only in the momentary — therefore it is pervaded by momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>). That [existence], being pervaded by that [momentariness], establishes momentariness in whatever substratum it is proved. Now this very [question] is examined: where is this pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) to be apprehended — in the example-substratum (<s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s>) or in the subject-substratum (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>)? Some say: in the example-substratum only, like smoke. Otherwise the inferential proof would be futile. Because the establishment of pervasion is necessarily consequent upon the establishment of both properties [in the example]. For when the pervasion of fire and smoke is established in the kitchen, one does not again seek the inferential mark of smoke for establishing fire. As follows:

children.translated_text: Pervasion is apprehended in the example, of two properties seen there;

children.text: hetumātrasya dṛṣṭasya vyāptiḥ pakṣe tu gamyate //
children.translated_text: when only the inferential mark (<s>hetu</s>) is seen in the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), the pervasion is [then] understood.
And that [pervasion], through universal applicability (<s>sarvopasaṃhāra</s>), rests upon the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>);
but the occurrence of that [universal] in the [particular] substratum is to be understood through inference.

body.text: pratyakṣadṛṣṭayorvanhidhūmayoḥ kāryyakāraṇabhāvasidvau tayorvyāptisidviriti pratyakṣasidve vanhau yuktamanumānavaiphalyam / naivaṃ vyāptisidveḥ prāk pramāṇāntarasidvaṃ dharmmiṇi kṣaṇikatvam / sādhanadharmmameva tu kevalamanupaśyanto viparyyaye bādhakapramāṇavalāttasya kṣaṇikatvena vyāptiṃ pratīmaḥ / tattataḥ sādhanavaiphalyam / vaiphalyameva, kṣaṇikatvavyāptasya sattvasya tathātvena dharmmiṇi pratītau kṣaṇikatvasyāpi pratīteriti cet / na / sarvvopasaṃhāravatī hi vyāptiḥ sādhyasidveraṅgam / tadiyamanapekṣitadharmmiviśeṣaṃ sādhanadharmmamātramavalambate / tadyathā / yatra dhūmastatrāgniriti / na punaryatra mahānase dhūmastatrāgniriti / evamihāpi yat sattatkṣaṇikamiti vyāptipratītau sādhanadharmmasyāpi dharmmiṇi sattvaṃ nāntarbhavati / kiṃ punaḥ sādhyadharmmasya / tasmāt sattvasāmānyasya sādhanadharmmasya pakṣadharmmatvaṃ vyāptiścaikaśaḥ pratipādya tadubhayasāmarthyāt sādhyadharmmasya dharmmiṇi vṛttiḥ pratīyata iti kuto 'numānavaiphalyaṃ / yadyevaṃ vyāptipratītāvasati dharmmiṇi parāmarśe sādhyadharmmiṇi vyāptigrahaṇamiti / kutaḥ / tatra dṛṣṭasya sattvasya vyāptipratīteḥ / yathā mahānasadṛṣṭāgnidhūmayorvyāptigrahe dṛṣṭāntadharmmiṇi vyāptigrahaṇamucyate / na hi vyāptigrahaṇe mahānasaparāmarśo 'stītyuktaṃ / nanu vyāptipakṣadharmmatvayorekaśaḥ pratītāvapi yasyaiva pakṣadharmmatvamavagatantasyaiva sādhyena vyāptiravasiteti sāmarthyāt sādhyasattākathanamavaiyarthyaṃ sādhanasya /
body.translated_text: When fire and smoke are seen by perception, the establishment of pervasion follows from the establishment of their cause-effect relationship — thus, it is appropriate that inference is futile when fire is established by perception. [Reply:] It is not so [in our case]: prior to the establishment of pervasion, momentariness in the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>) is not established by any other means of valid knowledge. Rather, seeing only the proving property (<s>sādhanadharma</s>) alone, we understand its pervasion by momentariness through the force of a counter-proof (<s>bādhaka</s>) that [demonstrates the impossibility of] the opposite. Therefore, there is [no] futility of the proof. [Objection:] There is indeed futility, because when existence (<s>sattva</s>), pervaded by momentariness, is cognized as such in the substratum, momentariness too would be cognized. [Reply:] No. For pervasion that involves universal applicability is a component of establishing the provable (<s>sādhya</s>). And this [pervasion] rests upon the proving property alone, without regard to any particular substratum. For example: 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire' — not 'wherever there is smoke in the kitchen, there is fire.' Similarly here too, in the cognition of pervasion 'whatever exists is momentary,' even the existence of the proving property in the substratum is not included. How much less the provable property (<s>sādhyadharma</s>). Therefore, the substratum-property (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>) of the proving property — namely, existence in general — and the pervasion are each established separately, and from the power of both together, the occurrence of the provable property in the substratum is understood. So how could there be futility of inference? [Objection:] If so, since in the cognition of pervasion there is a reference to the substratum in which existence is [observed], [this amounts to] apprehension of pervasion in the subject-substratum. [Reply:] How so? Because the pervasion of existence seen there is cognized. Just as when the pervasion of fire and smoke seen in the kitchen is apprehended, it is said that pervasion is apprehended in the example-substratum — for there is no reference to 'the kitchen' in the apprehension of pervasion, as has been stated. [Objection:] Even when the substratum-property and pervasion are cognized separately, it is understood that the very thing whose substratum-property is cognized is also pervaded by the provable — therefore, through that capacity, the statement of the existence of the provable is not futile for the proof.

body.text: nanu na pakṣadharmmatvagatiḥ sādhyagatiḥ sādhyadharmmasaṃsparśāt / nāpi vyāptipratītireva sādhyasidviḥ / sāmānyālambanatayā dharmmiviśeṣeṇa dharmmayoranavacchedāt / anyathā viśeṣayorvyāptiprasaṅgāt tadayaṃ vyastaviṣayaḥ sāmarthyāditi hetunirddeśaḥ / atha hetostrairūpyaparicchedasāmarthyāt sādhyapratītirutpadyata ityucyate / na tarhīdānīṃ vyarthohetuḥ / svarūpaniścayena sādhyaniścayopajananāt / na hi kvacidiyattādhikaṃ liṅgasya karttavyamastīti /
body.translated_text: Objection: The cognition of the property belonging to the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>) is not [itself] the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), because of its contact with the property of the probandum. Nor is the cognition of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) alone the establishment of the probandum, because — since it takes a universal as its object — the two properties are not delimited by the particular thesis-subject. Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence of pervasion between particulars. Therefore, the statement of the logical reason (<s>hetu</s>) has these two separately as its objects, through [their] collective efficacy. Now, if it is said that the cognition of the probandum arises from the capacity of ascertaining the three-fold character (<s>trairūpya</s>) of the reason — then the reason is not futile, since the ascertainment of its own nature generates the ascertainment of the probandum. For the inferential mark has nothing further to accomplish beyond this extent.

body.text: api ca gṛhīte pakṣadharmmatve sambandhe ca smṛte anumānaṃ bhavadbhiriṣyate / tadvadantarvyāptāvapīṣyatāṃ / na hi bahirvyāptivādināmapi vismṛtāyāṃ vyāptau anumānapravṛttirasti / tatra yasyaiva pakṣadharmmatvamavagataṃ tasyaiva sādhyadharmmeṇa vyāptismṛteḥ kinna sarvvānumānavaiyarthyaṃ / sādhyadharmmiṇo 'parāmarśeṇa vyāpteḥ smaraṇāditi cet / sādhyadharmmiṇi dṛṣṭasyaiva vyāptismaraṇe kathaṃ sādhyadharmmiṇo 'parāmarśaḥ / sāmānyālambanatvādvyāpteḥ / sādhyadharmmino 'navacchedāditi cet / nanu tatra dṛṣṭasya kathaṃ tenānavacchedaḥ / tenāvacchinnasya vā asādhāraṇatvāt kathaṃ vyāptiḥ / ayogavyavacchedena viśeṣaṇānnāsādhāraṇateti cet tathāpi kinna sādhyadharmmī parāmṛśyate / yatra yatra parvvate dhūmastatra tatrāgniryathā mahānasa iti sāmānyālambanāyāṃ vyāptau dharmmiviśeṣaparāmarśasyānaṅgatvāditi cet yuktametat sādhyadharmmiṇā hyayogavyavacchedaḥ sādhanadharmmasya rūpāntarameva pakṣadhammatvākhyaṃ / na tvayaṃ vyāpteraṅgaṃ / tamantareṇāpi vyāpteḥ sāmānyālambanāyāḥ paricchedaparisamāpteḥ kathamanyathā dṛṣṭāntadharmmiṇi vyāptigrahaṇavārttāpi tadedānīṃ pakṣadharmmatvāyogāt pakṣadharmmatvāgrahaṇāt; pakṣadharmmatvagrahaṇe vā tadaiva sādhyamapi sāmarthyādasidvaṃ sidvamiti sarvvānumānavaiyarthyaprasaṅgaḥ / paścātkālabhāviliṅgajñānamapi ca smṛtireva syāt na pramāṇaṃ / tasmāt vyāpteranaṅgatvāt pakṣadharmmatvaṃ vyāptigrahaṇe sadapi nāntarbhavatīti pṛthaggṛhītasmṛtayoḥ pakṣadharmmatvavyāptyoḥ sāmarthyādanumeyagatirutpadyate iti / evamavaiyarthyaṃ sādhanānāmeṣitavyam iti mānaphalatvāt / tadvat pṛthagmūtayoḥ pakṣadharmmatvavyāptyoḥ sāmarthyādanumānotpattirantarvyāptāvapi kinneṣyate / tadiṣṭau vā kathaṃ sādhanavaiyarthyaṃ / trairūpyagatisāmarthyādanumeyagatiriti hi tadupādānaśaktireva sāmarthyamucyate, na tu trairupyapratīterantarbhāva iti sarvvaṃ samānaṃ / na sarvvaṃ samānaṃ / antarvyāptau hi vyāptiṃ prati gatyaiva pakṣadharmmatvamavagataṃ anavagate pakṣadharmmatve vyāpterapyanavagateḥ / tato vyāptipūrvvake sādhanavāhye pakṣadharmmavacanamanarthakamanantavyāptau / naivaṃ bahirvyāptau bahireva vyāptigrahaṇāt / atrāha,-
body.translated_text: Moreover, you accept that inference occurs when the property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>) has been grasped and the relation (<s>sambandha</s>) has been recalled. Likewise, let it be accepted in the case of internal pervasion (<s>antarvyāpti</s>) too. For even for the proponents of external pervasion (<s>bahirvyāpti</s>), when pervasion is forgotten, inference does not proceed. If the pervasion with the probandum's property is recalled for the very same [reason] whose thesis-property has been cognized, why is not all inference rendered futile? If it be said: because pervasion is recalled without engaging the thesis-subject — [we reply:] how can there be non-engagement with the thesis-subject when pervasion is recalled for what was seen in the thesis-subject? If it be said: because pervasion takes a universal as its object and is not delimited by the thesis-subject — then how is there non-delimitation by the subject in which it was observed? Or if delimited by it, how can there be pervasion, since it would be uncommon? If it be said: it is not uncommon because of exclusion from non-occurrence as a qualifier — even so, why is the thesis-subject not engaged? If it be said: because in the pervasion taking a universal as its object — 'wherever there is smoke on a mountain, there is fire, as in a kitchen' — the engagement with the particular thesis-subject is irrelevant — this is correct. For the exclusion from non-occurrence with the thesis-subject is indeed just another form of the probative property called <s>pakṣadharmatva</s>. But this is not a component of pervasion, since the ascertainment of pervasion — which takes a universal as its object — is complete even without it. How else could there even be talk of grasping pervasion in the example-subject? But then, since <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> has not been established due to non-connection with the thesis, and since <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> has not been grasped — or if <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> has been grasped, then the probandum too has already been established through [the reason's] efficacy — there would be the unwanted consequence that all inference is futile. Moreover, the cognition of the inferential mark occurring later [than pervasion] would be mere memory, not a valid means of knowledge. Therefore, since <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> is not a component of pervasion, even though it is present when pervasion is grasped, it does not fall within [pervasion]. Hence, the cognition of the object of inference arises from the collective efficacy of <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> and <s>vyāpti</s>, which are separately grasped and recalled. Thus the non-futility of the means of proof should be maintained, since it has the status of a means of valid cognition. Likewise, why should it not be accepted in the case of internal pervasion too that inference arises from the collective efficacy of <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> and <s>vyāpti</s>, which are separately known? Or if that is accepted, how is the means of proof futile? For when it is said that the cognition of the object of inference arises from the efficacy of the cognition of the three-fold character, what is called 'efficacy' is precisely the capacity for giving rise to that — it is not [the claim that] the cognition of the three-fold character is internally contained [in inference]. Thus everything is the same [for both views]. [Opponent:] Not everything is the same. For in the case of internal pervasion, <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> is already cognized in the very act of cognizing pervasion, since pervasion cannot be cognized when <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> has not been cognized. Therefore, in a proof-statement preceded by pervasion, the statement of the thesis-property is purposeless in the case of internal pervasion. This is not so in the case of external pervasion, since pervasion is grasped externally. To this he replies:

children.translated_text: When a proof is presented by whatever means,
the property of the thesis-subject is to be understood, and afterward pervasion is cognized.

children.text: pratyakṣa iva dṛṣṭānte tatra setyanyathā kathaṃ /
children.translated_text: That [pervasion] exists there as if by direct perception in the example —

children.text: dvau dṛṣṭvā vidma iti ced vyāpteḥ prāk dvayadṛk kathaṃ //"
children.translated_text: otherwise, how [could it be known]? If it be said, 'we know by seeing both' — how can both be seen before pervasion?

body.text: vyāptipakṣadharmmatve hi svavākyābhyāṃ yena tena prayuktābhyāṃ sūcyete na tu sākṣāt pratīyete / vācaḥ svayamapramāṇatvāt / yadāha,-
body.translated_text: <s>Vyāpti</s> (pervasion) and <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> (thesis-property) are merely indicated by their respective propositions, presented in whatever order — they are not directly perceived. For words themselves are not valid means of knowledge. As [the author] says:

body.text: śaktasya sūcakaṃ heturvaco 'śaktamapi svayamiti / sūcitayo 'stu tayoḥ sattve hetau prathamatarapakṣadharmmatvaviṣayameva pramāṇamabhimukhībhavatu / tena pramāṇena dharmmiṇi sidvasya sattvasya paścādvyāptiḥ pramāṇāntareṇa gṛhyata iti kasya vaiyarthyamiti / pratyakṣe 'pi dṛṣṭāntadharmmiṇi prathamaṃ heturgṛhyate paścādvyāptirityeṣa eva kramaḥ anyathā dṛṣṭāntadharmmiṇi vyāptirgṛhītetyetadeva na syāt / dṛṣṭāntadharmmiṇyadṛṣṭasyaiva hetorvyāptigrahaṇāt / yadyevaṃ sādhyadharmmo 'pi vyāptigrahaṇādhikaraṇe dharmmiṇi grahītabya eva yathā vanhidhūmayoriti cet / na / tatra dṛṣṭasya hetorvipakṣe bādhakavṛttimātrādeva vyāptisidveḥ / jñātaścaivaṃ na khalu vyāptigrahaṇāt prāk kṣaṇikasya kvacidapi sidvirasti tasyānumeyatvāt / asidvāyāñca vyāptāvanumānāpravṛtteḥ / sādhanāntarasya ca tadarthamananusaraṇāt / anusaraṇe 'pyanavasthā syāt / avasthāne tāvat prayāsasya vaiyarthyāt / viaparyyaye vyāptibalādeva vyāptisidveravighātāt / vanhidhūmayostu nādṛṣṭayoḥ kāryyakāraṇabhāvasidveḥ / tatsidvau na vipakṣe bādhakavṛttiriti dvayadarśanavyapekṣā? vanhidhūmayorvyāptisidviḥ sattvakṣaṇikatvayostu naivaṃ / yathoktanyāyena vyāptisidveḥ / tasmāt sattvamātrasya tatra dharmmiṇi sidvasya bādhakavaśādvyāptiḥ setsyatītyeṣitavyaṃ / tadvadantarvyāptāvapi / te ime vyāptipakṣadharmmatve svasvapramāṇavyavacchedyasādhanavākye na tu kevalaṃ sūcayitavye / na cānyataravākyena śakyamubhayaṃ sūcayitumiti kuto 'nyataravākyavaiyarthyaṃ //
body.translated_text: [Objection:] The probans (<s>hetu</s>) is merely an indicator of the capable [probandum]; speech too is itself incapable [of causing the fire, etc.]. [Reply:] Let the existence of both in the probans, once indicated, be [established such that] the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is directed first toward the subject-property (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>). By that means of knowledge, the existence [of the probans] in the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) being established, pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is subsequently grasped by another means of knowledge—so where is the redundancy? Even in the case of direct perception, in the example-subject (<s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s>), the probans is first grasped and pervasion afterwards—this is indeed the order. Otherwise, the very fact that 'pervasion in the example-subject has been grasped' would not obtain, because pervasion is grasped of a probans that had not [yet] been observed in the example-subject. If so, should not the <s>sādhyadharma</s> (probandum-property) also be grasped in the subject where pervasion is grasped, as in the case of fire and smoke? No—because in that case, the establishment of pervasion follows merely from the restricting operation [of the reductio] (<s>bādhaka</s>) [applied to] the probans observed in the counter-instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>). And it is known thus: indeed, prior to the grasping of pervasion, there is no establishment anywhere of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>), since it is to be inferred. And when pervasion is not established, inference does not function. Nor does one pursue another means of proof for that purpose. And even if one did pursue it, there would be infinite regress. And if one were to stop [at some point], the [initial] effort would be pointless. In the opposite case, because the establishment of pervasion through the force of pervasion itself would not be obstructed. But in the case of fire and smoke, the causal relationship is not established when they are unobserved. And when that [causal relationship] is established, [one asks]: is it the restricting operation in the counter-instance [that establishes it]? [If so], the establishment of pervasion of fire and smoke requires the observation of both. But for existence (<s>sattva</s>) and momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>), it is not so, because pervasion is established by the method just stated. Therefore, one should expect that the pervasion of mere existence, which is established in that subject, will be established through the force of the reductio—likewise in the case of internal pervasion (<s>antarvyāpti</s>). These two—pervasion and the subject-property—are each to be delimited by their own respective means of valid cognition in the proof-statement; they are not merely to be indicated [together]. And since it is not possible to indicate both by a single statement, how can either statement be redundant?

children.translated_text: For the ascertainment of the threefold nature of a single property [occurs] successively;
since inference is absent when [any of these] is forgotten, how can any part of inference be pointless?

body.text: api ca saṃgrahaślokaḥ,-
body.translated_text: Moreover, a summary verse:

children.translated_text: If the probandum is established through the reductio [alone], then the grasping of another probans is pointless.
If the probandum is not established through the reductio, then the grasping of another subject is pointless.

body.text: yadi hi dharmmiṇi vyāptiḥ sidhyantyeva sādhyasidvimantarbhāvayati / nanu lābha evaiṣaḥ / byāptiprasādhakādeva pramāṇāt sādhyasidveḥ sattvahetvapāśrayaṇaprayāsasya nirasanāt / na hi vyasanamevaitalliṅgāntarānusaraṇaṃ nāma / atha na vyāptisādhakāt sādhyasidviḥ / na tarhyantarvyāptau hetuvaiyarthyamiti kimakāṇḍakātaratayā bahu taramāyāsamāviśasi / dvayaṃ hi bhavataḥ sādhyaṃ dṛṣṭāntadharmmiṇi vṛttiḥ sādhyadharmmiṇi ca / yathākramaṃ byāptipakṣadharmmatvayoḥ sidvyarthaṃ / nanu yadā pratiniyate dharmmiṇi vivādaḥ, tadvahirbhūte ca dharmmiṇi vyāptigrahaṇaṃ tadānīṃ bhavedvaiyarthyaṃ / yadā tu vastumātre vivādaḥ tadā sarvvavastuṣu hetorvṛttistvayāpi sādhyā mayāpi ceti katamasmin dharmmiṇi hetorvṛttisādhanaṃ mama vyarthaṃ bhaviṣyati / kathamidānīṃ bahirvyāptirvivādādhikaraṇaṃ bhūta evānyatamasmin vyāptisādhanāt / tāvanmātralakṣaṇatvācca sādhyadharmmiṇaḥ / bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ pravarttamānamantargatamapi dharmmiṇaṃ bahiṣkarotīti cet etadeva kathaṃ bhavatu bādhakena pravarttamānenaiva tasmin sādhyasādhanāt / sādhyasaṃśayopagame sādhyadharmmiṇi lakṣaṇopagamāditi cet ayuktametat / bādhakamātrāt na sādhyasidvirityasminpakṣe dharmmyantaraparigrahavaiyarthyābhidhānāt / bādhakāt sādhyasidvirityasmiṃstu pakṣe sādhanavaiyarthyamāpāditaṃ / tasmādvādhakamātreṇa sādhyāsidvau na kvacit sandehanivṛttiḥ / sandehānivṛttau na vahiṣkaraṇamavahiṣkṛtaśca sādhyadharmmyeveti tatra vyāptirantarvyāptireva nedānīṃ bahirvyāptervārttāpi / tadiyaṃbahirvyāptiramusmin pakṣe kathaṃ bhavati yadi pratiniyate dharmmiṇi vivādaḥ / tadvahirbhūte ca dharmmiṇi vyāptigrahaṇambhavati / tatra ca durudvaraḥ dharmmyantaraparigrahavaiyarthyadoṣaḥ / bādhakamātreṇa tu sādhyasidvau hetyantarameva vyarthaṃ / api ca satvahetorviśeṣeṇa na vahirvyāptisambhavaḥ /
body.translated_text: For if the pervasion, being established in the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>), includes within itself the establishment of the provable (<s>sādhya</s>) — [Objection:] well, this is a gain indeed! Because the effort of resorting to the existence-proof (<s>sattvahetu</s>) is rendered unnecessary, since the provable is established from the very means of valid knowledge that establishes the pervasion. For it is not at all a defect to pursue a different inferential mark. [Reply:] But if the provable is not established from the pervasion-establisher alone, then there is no futility of the inferential mark in internal pervasion — so why do you trouble yourself so excessively with this groundless agitation? For you have two things to prove in the example-substratum: the occurrence [of the proving property] there and [its occurrence] in the subject-substratum — for the purpose of establishing pervasion and substratum-property (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>), respectively. [Objection:] When the dispute concerns a specific substratum, and the apprehension of pervasion is in a substratum external to it, then there would be futility. But when the dispute concerns things in general, then the occurrence of the inferential mark in all things must be proved by you as well as by me — so in which substratum would my proof of the mark's occurrence be futile? How then is external pervasion [different], since it too establishes pervasion in just one of [the substrata] that constitute the locus of dispute? And because the subject-substratum is defined merely by that extent [of the dispute]. [Objection:] The counter-proof (<s>bādhaka</s>), when operating, excludes even the substratum included [within its scope]. [Reply:] Then how could it be otherwise? For the provable is established precisely in that [substratum] by the very operation of the counter-proof. [Objection:] Because in admitting that the provable is doubtful, there is acceptance of the definition of the subject-substratum. [Reply:] This is inappropriate. In the position that the provable is not established merely from the counter-proof, it has been stated that the resort to another substratum is futile. But in the position that the provable is established from the counter-proof, the futility of the proof has been demonstrated. Therefore, when the provable is not established merely by the counter-proof, there is nowhere any removal of doubt. When doubt is not removed, there is no exclusion [of the substratum from the subject]; and what is not excluded is indeed the subject-substratum — so the pervasion there is precisely internal pervasion (<s>antarvyāpti</s>), and there is not even any mention of external pervasion. Thus, how can this external pervasion obtain in this position if the dispute concerns a specific substratum? And the apprehension of pervasion occurs in a substratum external to it. And there the defect of futility of resorting to another substratum is irremediable. But when the provable is established merely from the counter-proof, another inferential mark itself is futile. Moreover, for the existence-proof (<s>sattvahetu</s>) in particular, external pervasion is not possible:

children.translated_text: When the existence of the substratum is not established, there is no occasion for dispute;
and when [existence] is not established there, apprehension of pervasion in the subject-substratum —

body.text: vyāptigrahaḥ kathaṃ nasyāddṛṣṭānte 'pi na vā bhavet //
body.translated_text: how would that apprehension of pervasion not occur? Or would it not occur even in the example?

body.text: yatra hi dharmmiṇi dṛṣṭasya hetorvyāptiḥ pratīyate tatra tasya vyāptigrahaṇamākhyāyate / dṛṣṭañca sādhyadharmmiṇi sattvamanyathā vimatyayogāditi kathaṃ nāntarvyāptiḥ /
body.translated_text: For wherever the pervasion of the inferential mark seen in a substratum is cognized, there its apprehension of pervasion is declared. And existence is seen in the subject-substratum — otherwise there would be no occasion for dispute — so how is this not internal pervasion?

body.text: tathāpi sādhanavaiyarthyaniṣedhāya bahireva gṛhṇīma iti cet tat kimidānīṃ tvadicchānurodhāt dharmmiṇi hetorddarśanamadarśanamastu / darśanaviśeṣe vā bahireva vyāptigrahaṇavyavasthāstu / ubhayatra dṛṣṭasya vyāptigrahaṇe 'pyasti bahirvyāptibhāga iti cet / nanu kimarthamiyān bhāgo yatnena saṃrakṣyate /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Even so, to prevent the futility of the proof, let us apprehend [pervasion] externally only. [Reply:] Then what? Should the seeing or non-seeing of the inferential mark in the substratum be determined by compliance with your wish? Or should there be a fixed determination that pervasion is apprehended only externally when there is a specific kind of seeing? Even when pervasion is apprehended for [a property] seen in both [subject and example], is there still a portion of external pervasion? [Objection:] Indeed. [Reply:] But then, for what purpose is this much [of external pervasion] so carefully preserved?

body.text: mābhūt hetuvaiyarthyamiti cet / nanu yadi bādhakavṛttimātreṇa vyāptigrahaṇādhikaraṇe dharmmiṇi sādhyasidveḥ sādhanavaiyarthyamantarvyāptau tadetadvahirvyāptāvapi tulyaṃ / tasmād vyasanamātraṃ bahirvyāptigrahaṇe viśeṣeṇa sattve hetau kevalaṃ jaḍadhiyāmeva niyamena dṛṣṭāntasāpekṣaḥ sādhanaprayogaḥ paritoṣāya jāyate / teṣāmevānugrahārthamācāryyo dṛṣṭāntamupādatte /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Lest there be futility of the inferential mark. [Reply:] But if, merely from the operation of the counter-proof, there is futility of the proof because the provable is established in the substratum that is the locus of pervasion-apprehension — this is the same in external pervasion as in internal pervasion. Therefore, the apprehension of external pervasion is merely an [unnecessary] trouble. Specifically, when existence is the inferential mark, the inferential procedure that depends on an example is necessarily for the satisfaction of the dull-witted alone. It is for their benefit alone that the master (<s>ācārya</s>) adduces an example:

body.text:
yat sattatkṣaṇikaṃ yathā ghaṭa iti /
paṭumatayastu naivaṃ dṛṣṭāntamapekṣante /
body.translated_text:
'Whatever exists is momentary, like a pot.'
But those of sharp intellect do not depend on an example in this way.

children.translated_text: "Therefore, from among the stated examples, he mentioned the pot as an example;
similarly, since there is non-futility in the means of valid knowledge, let [the same] be accepted in internal pervasion too."

body.text: ityantaraślokaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is an interpolated verse.

body.text: kathamidānīṃ anumeye sattvameva sattvameva sapakṣa eva sattvamasapakṣe vāsattvameva niścitamiti hetostrairupyamavagantavyam /
body.translated_text: How, then, is the threefold character (<s>trairūpya</s>) of the reason to be understood — namely, that there is existence in the subject of inference, existence only in the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>), and non-existence only in the dissimilar instance (<s>asapakṣa</s>)?

children.translated_text: "In the intellect, the similar and dissimilar instances — endowed with and devoid of the probandum-property —

children.text: sattvāsattve tatra hetoste grāhye yatra tatra vā //"
children.translated_text: the existence and non-existence of the reason therein are to be grasped, wherever [possible]."

body.text: sādhyadharmmayuktaḥ sarvvaḥ sāmānyena sapakṣaḥ, atadyuktaścāsapakṣa iti / tasmin sapakṣa eva sattvamasapakṣe cāsattvameva yathākramamanvayavyatirekau tau punaryatra tatra vā dharmmiṇi grahītavyau yatra śakyau grahītum /
body.translated_text: Everything that is endowed with the probandum-property is, in general, the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>); and what is devoid of it is the dissimilar instance (<s>asapakṣa</s>). The existence [of the reason] only in the similar instance and its non-existence only in the dissimilar instance are, respectively, the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). These two, in turn, are to be grasped in whatever subject (<s>dharmin</s>) they can be grasped.

body.text: tadiha sattvasya sarvvato 'kṣaṇikādvyāvṛttau bādhakabalāt sidvāyāṃ yat sattat kṣaṇikameveti anvayaḥ sādhyadharmmiṇyavagṛhyate / tatra dṛṣṭasya hetorvyāptigrahaṇāt dharmmyantarāsambhavāt / sambhave 'pi tadanusaraṇavaiyarthyāt / yadyevamasādhāraṇo nāma kathamanaikāntika uktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, since the exclusion of existence (<s>sattva</s>) from everything non-momentary is established by the force of the counter-proof (<s>bādhaka</s>), the positive concomitance — 'whatever exists is momentary' — is apprehended in the very subject of the probandum. Because the pervasion of the reason that is observed there is grasped; because there is no other subject [to serve as an example]; and even if there were, because pursuing it would be pointless. But if this is so, [and the reason is] exclusive (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>), how has it been called inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>)?

children.translated_text: The defect of exclusiveness (<s>asādhāraṇatā</s>) in the reason was stated with regard to the confused [thinkers],
because of their failure to grasp pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>); it is not so when there is universal applicability (<s>sarvopasaṃhāra</s>).

body.text: uktametajjaḍadhiyo dharmmyantara eva vyāptigrahaṇaṃ pratipannāḥ / tadabhimānāpekṣayāsādhāraṇamanaikāntikamāha śrāvaṇatvaṃ dṛṣṭāntābhāvāt / sādhyadharmmiṇi ca vyāptiraniṣṭeragṛhītāyāṃ vyāptau sandigdhobhayatayāniścayakaratvāt / athavā asādhāraṇataiva śrāvaṇatvasya mūḍhābhimānopakalpitā / dṛṣṭaiva hi śabdavyaktidharmmiṇī vivādādhikaraṇāt / anyathā dharmmyasidviprasaṅgācca / dṛṣṭādṛṣṭaśabdavyaktisādhāraṇañca śrāvaṇatvaṃ hetuḥ / dhūmasāmānyavat / tataḥ sarvvopasaṃhāravatyāḥ vyāpteḥ sambhavāt sattvādivadadṛṣṭameva sādhanaṃ śrāvaṇatvākhyaṃ / kramayaugapadyānupalambha eva cātra bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ / śrotrajñānajana katvameva hi śrāvaṇatvaṃ / tasmānmūḍhavyapekśayāsādhāraṇatvāt / asādhāraṇasya sarvvopasaṃhārāyogāt / sādhya dharmmiṇi vyāptipratītāveva sādhyapratīteḥ sādhanavaiphalyaṃ syādeva / tanmābhūvvaiphalyamiti naiva vyāptirgrahītavyā / tasyāmagṛhītāyāṃ sandigdhobhayatayā syādanaikāntikatvaṃ / sarvvopasaṃhāreṇa tu vyāptigrahaṇe yathoktanyāyena sādhanavaiphalyābhāvāt / aduṣṭaṃ sattvādi sādhanameveti veditavyam / tadevamubhayathā mūḍhajanāpekṣayāsādhāraṇamanaikāntikamuktam /
body.translated_text: This has been stated: those of dull intellect have accepted that pervasion is grasped only in a different subject [i.e., an example]. With regard to their assumption, [the author] called the exclusive [reason] inconclusive — [e.g.,] audibility (<s>śrāvaṇatva</s>), because of the absence of an example. And since, for those who do not accept [it], pervasion in the subject of the probandum is not grasped — because of the doubt about both [presence and absence], it fails to produce certainty. Alternatively, the exclusiveness of audibility itself is fabricated by the false assumption of the confused. For the particular sound-instance that is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is indeed observed, since it is the locus of the dispute. Otherwise, the unwanted consequence of an unestablished subject (<s>dharmyasiddhi</s>) would follow. And audibility is a reason common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) to both observed and unobserved sound-instances, like the universal 'smoke-ness.' Therefore, since pervasion with universal applicability is possible, audibility — like existence (<s>sattva</s>) and the like — is an unexemplified (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) but valid proof. And here the non-apprehension of succession and simultaneity (<s>kramayaugapadyānupalambha</s>) itself is the counter-proof (<s>bādhaka</s>). For audibility is precisely the property of being produced by auditory cognition. Therefore, because of [being called] exclusive only with regard to the confused; because the exclusive [reason] does not admit of universal applicability; because if pervasion were cognized in the very subject of the probandum then the probandum too would be cognized and the proof would be futile — so, lest there be futility, pervasion should not be grasped at all; and when it is not grasped, there would be inconclusiveness due to doubt about both [presence and absence]. But when pervasion is grasped through universal applicability, there is no futility of the proof according to the method stated. Therefore, existence (<s>sattva</s>) and the like should be known as valid, unflawed proofs. Thus, in both ways [i.e., from two perspectives], the exclusive [reason] has been called inconclusive with regard to confused people.

body.text: samānañcaitadvahirvyāptivādināmapi yadi hi mūḍhamatāpekṣā na syāt syādeva śrāvaṇatvamaduṣṭo hetuḥ / satvādivanniyataśabdeṣu hi vivāde śabdāntaraṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: And this is the same even for the proponents of external pervasion (<s>bahirvyāptivādin</s>). For if there were no regard for the views of the confused, audibility would indeed be a valid, unflawed reason. For in a dispute about sounds determined [to be momentary or not], like existence (<s>sattva</s>) and the like, there would be another sound [to serve as an example].

body.text: dṛṣṭāntaḥ sarvvaśabdeṣu vigatau bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ pravarttammanaṃ adṛṣṭāntamapi tatraikaṃ dṛṣṭāntayatīti kathama sādhāraṇamanaikāntikaṃ veti / 0 /
body.translated_text: The example serves for all sounds; and when [pervasion] is absent [in them], the counter-proof (<s>bādhaka pramāṇa</s>) operates; [and it] makes even an unexemplified [reason] into an exemplified one for that [purpose] — so how can [audibility] be called an exclusive inconclusive [reason]?

body.text: antarvyāptisamarthanaṃ samāptamiti // 0 //
body.translated_text: The <s>Antarvyāptisamarthana</s> (Establishment of Internal Pervasion) is concluded.

body.text: kṛtiriyaṃ ratnākaraśāntipādānāmiti // 0 //
body.translated_text: This is the work of the venerable <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>.
